title: Guillain-Barré syndrome
presentation: Progressive, symmetric, ascending limb weakness and sensory loss over days to 4 weeks, with absent or depressed deep tendon reflexes. May include facial/bulbar weakness, ophthalmoplegia (Miller Fisher), or dysautonomia
definitions: Classic GBS (AIDP): sensorimotor, ascending, demyelinating on NCS
AMAN / AMSAN: motor or sensorimotor axonal variants; often post-Campylobacter; IgG anti-GM1, GM1b, GD1a, GalNAc-GD1a (Willison & Yuki 2002)
Miller Fisher syndrome (MFS): triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, areflexia; anti-GQ1b in up to 90% (Leonhard 2019)
Pharyngeal-cervical-brachial (PCB): ptosis, facial, bulbar and arm weakness with leg sparing; IgG anti-GT1a (± GQ1b) (Willison & Yuki 2002)
Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis: MFS features plus impaired consciousness and pyramidal signs, often overlapping with GBS; IgG anti-GQ1b/GT1a (Leonhard 2019; Willison & Yuki 2002)
Albuminocytological dissociation: elevated CSF protein with normal WBC (<50/mcL); may be ABSENT in the first week (~50% normal early)

immediateActions.action: Assess respiratory and bulbar status immediately: bedside forced vital capacity (FVC), negative inspiratory force (NIF), single-breath count, neck flexion strength, swallowing
Apply the '20/30/40 rule' for ICU admission / elective intubation threshold: FVC <20 mL/kg, NIF worse than -30 cmH2O, max inspiratory pressure <40 cmH2O, or single-breath count <15
Continuous cardiac telemetry and frequent vital signs for dysautonomia (wide BP fluctuations, bradyarrhythmias, tachyarrhythmias)
Initiate IVIG or PLEX early if non-ambulatory, rapidly progressive, or respiratory/bulbar involvement. DO NOT delay treatment for EMG/NCS if clinical picture is convincing

notes: Every 4h if progressing; q2h if borderline; single-breath count if spirometry unavailable

workup.test: Lumbar puncture (CSF cell count, protein, glucose)
notes: Protein typically elevated with WBC <5/mcL (up to 50 allowed; >50 suggests HIV, Lyme, sarcoid, or leukemia); protein may be NORMAL in first 3–7 days (re-tap in 1–2 weeks if diagnosis in doubt)
Aids subtype classification (AIDP vs AMAN); prolonged distal latencies, conduction block, temporal dispersion, absent F-waves early; normal early study does NOT rule out GBS

indication: Miller Fisher (GQ1b), AMAN/AMSAN (GM1, GD1a), atypical variants
notes: Send before IVIG or PLEX if possible; do not wait for results to treat
Limited, assay-dependent value; a negative result doesn't exclude GBS; most useful when MFS is suspected (Leonhard 2019)

workup.test: MRI cervical spine (± whole spine) with gadolinium
indication: Sensory level, asymmetric findings, brisk reflexes, urinary retention at presentation (rule out cord compression / myelitis)
notes: GBS may show prominent anterior spinal root enhancement

workup.test: Infectious triggers panel (Campylobacter, CMV, EBV, HIV, Mycoplasma, hepatitis)
notes: Stool culture / PCR for Campylobacter if diarrhea in prior 4 weeks

treatment.doseText: 0.4 g/kg/day IV for 5 consecutive days (total 2 g/kg); alternative: 1 g/kg/day for 2 days
notes: Equally effective to plasma exchange; preferred for ease of administration and hemodynamic stability
Pre-screen: baseline IgA level (severe IgA deficiency risks anaphylaxis, though rare); renal function (renal tubular necrosis risk with sucrose-containing formulations)
Premedicate: acetaminophen 650 mg PO + diphenhydramine 25–50 mg IV/PO 30 min before infusion
Hydrate adequately before and during infusion to reduce thrombotic and renal risk

treatment.doseText: 4–5 exchanges (200–250 mL plasma/kg total, ~40–50 mL/kg per exchange) over 7–14 days, using 5% albumin replacement
notes: Equal efficacy to IVIG; preferred if IVIG contraindicated (severe IgA deficiency, hypercoagulability, acute renal failure)
Requires central venous access (dialysis catheter / apheresis line); risk of hypotension, hypocalcemia, line sepsis
DO NOT combine IVIG and PLEX — sequential combination showed no additional benefit in RCTs
evidenceNote: Cochrane Review 2017; Plasma Exchange/Sandoglobulin GBS Trial Group

treatment.doseText: Do NOT use — corticosteroids alone show NO benefit and may delay recovery (Cochrane 2016)
notes: Multiple RCTs confirmed that neither oral nor IV steroids improve outcomes in GBS
If considering steroids, reconsider the diagnosis (e.g., CIDP, transverse myelitis, vasculitis)

treatment.doseText: Enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily (or UFH 5,000 U SC q8–12h) + pneumatic compression devices while non-ambulatory
notes: High risk of DVT/PE due to prolonged immobility

treatment.doseText: Gabapentin 300 mg TID (titrated up), pregabalin 75 mg BID, or duloxetine 30–60 mg daily
notes: Severe back/limb pain occurs in up to 80% of GBS patients, often preceding weakness

pitfalls: Giving corticosteroids: Cochrane evidence confirms steroids do not benefit and may worsen GBS
Waiting for elevated CSF protein or diagnostic EMG before starting therapy — both can be completely normal in the first week
Relying on pulse oximetry to judge respiratory failure — hypoxia is a VERY LATE sign in neuromuscular respiratory failure; vital capacity drops long before SpO2 falls
Succinylcholine is CONTRAINDICATED for intubation — risks life-threatening hyperkalemic cardiac arrest due to up-regulated denervation acetylcholine receptors
Failing to recognize dysautonomia — wide swings from severe hypertension to sudden bradycardic arrest can occur without warning; avoid aggressive antihypertensives
escalateWhen: FVC <20 mL/kg, NIF worse than -30 cmH2O, or single-breath count <15 → urgent ICU transfer and intubation readiness
New or worsening bulbar weakness (dysphagia, weak cough, aspiration risk)
Hemodynamic instability: sustained bradycardia (<40 bpm), pause >3 sec, or SBP swings >60 mm Hg
Rapid motor decline: loss of ambulation within 24–48 hours (predicts respiratory failure via EGRIS)
institutionVaries: Choice of first-line therapy (IVIG stocked and readily available at most centers; PLEX requires apheresis team and line placement)
ICU bed criteria: some centers admit all confirmed GBS to ICU/stepdown; others allow ward monitoring if stable and ambulatory
